ruling.reasoning:
The quote was $12.71 at surge 1x and the trip ran at 1.4x, so the fare rose $3.46 above the quote, with the surge part equal to (1.4 − 1) × $10.66 = $4.26, capped at the $3.46 excess [F6][F7][F8][SURGE-2]. The trace settles that surge rose between quote and trip start and that an in-app notice was sent at or before pickup [F8][F9][SURGE-2].

I read the notice text itself: "Fares are 1.4× higher right now. Your fare stays at the quoted $12.71. You can cancel for free." [F9] It states the new multiplier (1.4×), it states a revised estimated fare (the quoted $12.71), and it states free cancellation — all three items SURGE-1 requires [F9][SURGE-1]. The clause only asks that a revised estimated fare be stated; an estimate that differs from the fare finally charged is still a stated estimate, and the platform log outweighs the rider's assertion that no notice arrived [F9][SURGE-1]. The element [SURGE-1:notice] is therefore met.

Because the rider was notified and rode, SURGE-2 puts the higher fare on the rider: the surge differential is not refundable, and the outcome is no_action [F7][F9][SURGE-2]. No other charge is disputed — the distance billed (3.9 km) does not exceed the optimal route (3.9 km), so there is nothing to refund under the route rules [F1][F3], and the amounts reconcile: base $3.90 + distance $5.46 + time $1.30 + platform $1.25 = $16.17 [F5].

I read every text in the record — the two chat messages and the driver's written statement — and found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving allegation or expression of feeling unsafe: the messages are a pickup arrangement ("waiting at the kerb outside Mandarin Gallery, in a red cap" / "1 min away, white Honda Vezel") and a factual statement about the notice [F10][F11][F13]. The safety screen is "none" and does not change the path [SAFE-1].

The record is complete for what this ruling needs: GPS distances, a metered fare breakdown, the surge log with timestamp and full notice text, and a fully timestamped chat record [F1][F5][F9][F12]. No element remains undetermined, so the case can be ruled without a person [F12][TH-1][TH-3]. Both briefs in this ablation request no_action, which matches the outcome I reach independently [F14][F15].
